Please find enclosed today's edition of 'Hand-picked articles for you'

Ajla Muhamed

Delegation of the European Union

Sv. Kiril i Metodij, no. 52b, 1000 Skopje

( +389 2 3248 528


 

 

 

Hand-picked articles for you

                                   30 Mar 2022

 

 

Varhelyi will discuss dialogue with North Macedonia with Petkov in Sofia

EU Enlargement Commissioner Oliver Varhelyi will visit Bulgaria in the coming days, Bulgarian government spokeswoman Lena Borislavova confirmed today. She added that among the topics with Prime Minister Kiril Petkov, will be Bulgaria's dialogue with North Macedonia.

EU Special Representative for the Belgrade-Pristina Dialogue, Miroslav Lajcak, backed the position of the head of the Bundestag Foreign Affairs Committee that Brussels should start membership negotiations with Skopje and Tirana. His tweet was in response to a statement by Michael Roth, the German Foreign Minister at the German Foreign Ministry, who had previously written that the EU must "fulfil its promises: start of accession talks with Albania, North Macedonia, visa liberalization for Kosovo"./Time.mk

 

 

Ø Census results

 

The European Commission applauded the 2021 Population and Housing Census in North Macedonia calling it a great achievement, MIA s Brussels correspondent reports.

 

EC Spokesperson Ana Pisonero said that the Census was a great achievement, as an updated population data are essential for planning and implementing appropriate social, demographic and economic policies for the benefit of all the citizens.

 

 

According to the Census 2021 results, presented today by the State Statistical Office Director Apostol Simovski, the total resident population of North Macedonia on 5 September 2021 was 1,836,713 inhabitants.

 

By ethnic affiliation, 58.44% of the population declared themselves as ethnic Macedonians, 24.30% as ethnic Albanians, 3.86% as ethnic Turks, 2.53% as Roma, 1.30% as ethnic Serbs, 0.87% as Bosniaks, 0.47% as Vlachs. For 7.20% of the resident population, data were taken from administrative sources. Other tiny ethnic groups listed in the results are Torbeshi (0.23%), Bulgarians (0.19%), Egyptians (0.13%), Croats (0.12%), Muslims, Montenegrins (0.6%), Greeks, Muslim Macedonians, Russians (0.2% each), English, Germans, Gorani, Poles, Romanians, Slovenes, Ukrainians (0.1% each)&

 

When it comes to the total enumerated population (also including the non-resident population, i.e. the Macedonian nationals living and residing abroad for more than one year and the foreigners temporarily living in the country for less than 12 months), there are 2,097,319 citizens, of whom 54.21% are ethnic Macedonians, 29.52% ethnic Albanians, 3.98% ethnic Turks, 2.34% Roma, 1.18% Serbs, 0.87% Bosniaks, 0.44% Vlachs, 1.06% others.... For 6.31% of the citizens (or 132,260), data were taken from administrative sources.  

 

SDSM commented that the Census, which was conducted after 20 years, is a great success for the citizens and the country. We are happy that the operation was completed successfully, for the first time in a combined manner and during a pandemic. Enumerating 99% of the population is a result that cannot achieve even many developed European countries.

 

VMRO-DPMNE stated that the Census results reveal alarming figures for all municipalities, except for the City of Skopje - there is excessive migration. While the government tends to present the Census as a success, the migration suggests it has failed. The figure of 7.2% undeclared (not enumerated) citizens shows that the Census is incomplete. The operation was conducted amid numerous remarks and lots of politics; hence, we consider that everyone is entitled to question the figures. We did not want to comment before the release of the official figures, but even before and during the release of the results, the government parties played (and are still playing) with percentages, which politicises the Census. In spite of having data in other registries for the 7.2% of the citizens (132,000), who boycotted the Census, the State Statistical Office did not use them to identify their ethnic affiliation. Most of the citizens who were not enumerated are (ethnic) Macedonians. In spite of its remarks, VMRO-DPMNE called on the citizens to get enumerated; unfortunately, there were certain actors who called for boycott and it came to the detriment of the census data, the completeness of the process and of (ethnic) Macedonians. The figure that 200,000 citizens left the country since 2002 is defeating, and speaks about the government s poor economic policies. VMRO-DPMNE commits to conducting a purely electronic and complete census, in line with all European standards, after coming to power.

 

DUI leader Ahmeti noted that the Census gave a clearer picture about the inhabitants in the country; the (ethnic) Albanians make 29.5% of the overall population, 24.3% of the resident population, and 22.8% of the Skopje population (compared to 20.4% in 2002). Congratulations to the institutions for the successfully completed work.

 

Alliance for Albanians said that according to the results, only 12% of the population live abroad while international organisations say it is about 30%. All this makes the entire process and the figures published today unreliable. The (ethnic) Macedonians remain a majority with 54% thanks to the manipulation done with the cancellation of the initial enumeration, which demobilised the (ethnic) Albanian citizens. The betrayal has a name and it is DUI.

 

Besa commented that one thing is obvious during the 20 year-rule of DUI and due to their poor policies over 10% of the (ethnic) Albanians have left their country.

 

Levica commented that this Census was a mere political operation orchestrated by DUI and approved of by SDSM. We have on many occasions elaborated why the Law on Census was problematic (it was smuggled with an EU flag, which is not the case in any country). We had enumeration of the diaspora, which is also not the case elsewhere. We had enumeration only on the basis of unique personal numbers, which is in breach with all international standards, or people providing personal data about others, which is banned by the international conventions ratified by the country. It is about literally forged and rigged results.

 

Democratic Union (part of the government coalition) said the results do not reflect the reality it is estimated that only 10% of the (ethnic) Macedonians in the diaspora were enumerated while in the country, over 130,000 people, mostly (ethnic) Macedonians, were not enumerated. This suggests that the Census is not successful and the reasons and responsibility should be sought. Many factors led to the Census s failure: destructive conduct and calls for boycott by some parties, poor preparations and methodology& We propose additional cross-checking of data, and an additional census for the non-resident population.

 

 

President Pendarovski meets Austrian EU Minister Edtstadler

North Macedonia s President Stevo Pendarovski met Wednesday with Austria s Federal Minister for the EU and the Constitution, Karolin Edtstadler, who is paying an official visit to the country.

In terms of the Austrian support for the European integration process of the country and the region, President Pendarovski and Minister Edtstadler pointed to an urgent need to effectuate the unconditional March 2020 decision of the EU s General Affairs Council to start the negotiating process, particularly after the latest developments in the wider neighbourhood and the geopolitical and security challenges on the European continent due to the Russia invasion of Ukraine. Pendarovski added that any further delay of the start of negotiations contributes to growth of Euroscepticism in the country and opens the door to increased influence of third parties, reads the press release.

 

·       Parliament Speaker Talat Xhaferi, met today with the Federal Minister for Europe and Constitutional Affairs of the Republic of Austria, Caroline Edstadler, who thanked her for her strong and open support to the Republic of Austria. integration of the country, as well as the entire Western Balkans in the European Union.

 

 

·       After their meeting, both Edtstadler and DPM for euro affairs Bojan Marichikj expressed optimism for a positive outcome of the dialogue with Bulgaria. The intensity of the negotiations has not decreased since January, Maricic claims, while protecting the Macedonian national interests.

 

- The results achieved in the historical commission should be announced by historians as direct participants. The general agreement between the governments of North Macedonia and Bulgaria and the results achieved by the Commission to be announced by the members of the Commission, and not by the governments, because that is fair and thus gives the historians the opportunity to announce - at what stage and what progress they have made, said Deputy Prime Minister Bojan Marichikj.

 

Edstadler, who recently visited Bulgaria and met with Petkov, said she saw positive moves forward by the Bulgarian government to resolve outstanding issues and reiterated support for the European aspirations of the Western Balkans, without specifying whether June was a date for raising of the Bulgarian veto.

 

The President of VMRO-DPMNE Hristijan Mickoski met with the Minister of Europe and Constitutional Affairs of Austria, Caroline Edstadler.  Mickoski stressed the gratitude to the Republic of Austria for giving North Macedonia continuous, sincere and unequivocal support  over the recent years, emphasizing that the clear support of North Macedonia's European integration is of particular importance, as a strategic priority of both the European Union and North Macedonia.

"VMRO-DPMNE, especially in these turbulent times for Europe, remains firmly on the European path, and is committed to starting negotiations with the EU immediately and without delay," Mickoski said.

 

EU accession Talks with Skopje without delay is Greece s strong demand, spokesman

Greece has once again reiterated its continuous support of the EU perspective of North Macedonia. Foreign Ministry spokesman Alexandros Papaioannou on Wednesday said that his country s demand is that EU accession negotiations should start immediately with North Macedonia./MIA;other

 

 

 

 

 

Other headlines:

·       Pendarovsski receives credentials of new Indian Ambassador

·       Infectious Diseases Commission recommends high schoolers stop wearing masks in Schools

·       Eight Austrian companies show interest to invest in road and railway

 

 

Best,

 

Ajla
